raw_response:
I am 63 years old and have farmed these 8 mu in Huaiqiao, Quzhou County for 40 years. I never went to school, but I know every corner of this land. My household is just my wife and me — two old people, two pairs of hands. We are not young anymore, so I keep the cropping simple. I do not grow winter wheat like some of my neighbors; the wheat-maize double crop is too much labour for the two of us. Instead, my system is spring maize and mungbean.

This year I will put 3 mu into mungbean and 5 mu into spring maize, same as last year. The mungbean goes in around the middle of April. It grows fast and I can harvest by mid-July, which gives me a bit of cash from the pods before the maize is even ready. I save my own mungbean seed — about 2 jin per mu — so I do not need to buy it. For the maize, I buy hybrid seed, Denghai 605, one package per mu. The hybrid vigor is worth the money; it gives me a solid harvest even if the summer weather turns dry.

For both crops I do rotary tillage to prepare the seedbed. I broadcast compound fertilizer as a basal dressing: 200 jin per mu of 15-15-15 for the maize, and 100 jin per mu of the same for the mungbean. That works out to about 15 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium per mu for the maize, and about 7.5 kg each per mu for the mungbean. I do not use manure anymore — hauling it is too hard for us at our age, and the chemical fertilizer is easier to spread.

We are lucky to have a well. I irrigate the maize four times by border irrigation, especially at jointing and grain filling. The mungbean only needs two irrigations; too much water and the pods will rot. For pests, I spray insecticide three times on the maize and once on the mungbean, and I add one herbicide spray on the maize to keep the weeds down. I also lay plastic film on the mungbean plot to keep the early spring soil warm and moist.

I expect the maize to yield around 540 kg per mu, and the mungbean about 90 kg per mu. I do not hire labour — it is just my wife and me doing the sowing, spraying, and harvesting. That is how we have always done it, and that is how we will do it this year.
